sentences.text: No. - 718 of 2010 Appellant :- Smt. Meera Devi And Others Respondent :- U.P.S.R.T.C. Thru A.R.M.

Deoria Depot Counsel for Appellant :- Vashistha Tiwari Counsel for Respondent :- Dinkar Mani Tripathi,Narendra Pratap Singh Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.
1.

Heard Sri Vashistha Tiwari, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri Dinkar Mani Tripathi,
learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent- U.P.S.R.T.C.
2.

This first appeal from order has been filed under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 on behalf of the claimants-appellants for enhancement of compensation against the judgment and award dated 08.12.2009 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Deoria in M.A.C.P. No.318 of 2007 (Smt. Meera Devi and others vs. U.P.S.R.T.C.), by which compensation of Rs.2,57,751/- along-with 6% interest has been awarded to the claimants-appellants on account of death of Yadunandan Tiwari aged about 38 years, who died in a road accident on 10.05.2007 and liability has been fixed upon respondent-U.P.S.R.T.C.
3.

1 Khadya Nigam and had earned Rs.7500/- per month.

sentences.text: The claimants have fully proved the income of the deceased as Rs.7,500/- per month and the Claims Tribunal has erred in accepting only Rs.24,000/- per annum as income of the deceased.
It is further submitted that there are four dependents on the income of the deceased and the Claims Tribunal has erred in deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased in place of 1/4th.

Lastly, it is submitted that nothing has been awarded towards future prospects and only Rs.9,500/- was awarded for non-pecuniary damages, whereas claimants are entitled for 40% future prospects and Rs.70,0000/- for non-pecuniary damages in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 S.C.C. 680.
4.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 S.C.C. 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No other ground has been pressed by learned counsel for appellants.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent submits that the compensation awarded by the claims tribunal is almost just and proper and no ground for enhancement is made out but he has not disputed the aforesaid legal grounds argued by learned counsel for appellants.
6.
Considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. The claims tribunal while deciding issue no.2 has recorded the finding that the claimants had failed to prove the income of the deceased as no authentic evidence has been filed by the claimants to prove the income of the deceased as Rs. 7500/- per month.

The income of the deceased was accepted as Rs. 24,000/- per annum accepting him as a labourer having income Rs. 100/- to 102/-
per day.

Record shows that the deceased was not engaged as labourer in Food Cooperation of India,
but was engaged as contract labourer by the contractor.

The income of the deceased as Rs. 24,000/-
per annum accepted by claims tribunal for the accident of year 2007 is unreasonable.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Laxmi Devi and others vs. Mohammad Tabber, reported in (2008) 12 S.C.C. 165 has provided the notional income of Rs. 3,000/- per month for the accident of 2004,
therefore, the income of the deceased is accepted as Rs. 3,000/- per month.

entities.text: Laxmi Devi and others vs. Mohammad Tabber, reported in (2008) 12 S.C.C. 165
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Claims Tribunal has also erred in deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses ignoring the fact that there are four dependents of the deceased and deduction would be 1/4 as per law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt.) vs. Delhi Road Transport Corporation, reported in (2009) 6 S.C.C.
121.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma (Smt.) vs. Delhi Road Transport Corporation, reported in (2009) 6 S.C.C.
121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The multiplier of 15 has rightly been applied by claims tribunal.
The claimants/appellants are also entitled for 40% future prospects and Rs. 70,000/- for non pecuniary damages as provided by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
8. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsels for the parties, the compensation awarded to the appellants is liable to be enhanced.

The compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is reassessed as below:-
I) Monthly income = Rs.3000/-
II) Annual income = Rs. 3,000/- X 12 = Rs.36,000/- III) Future prospects (40%) =
Rs.14,400/-
Smt. Meera Devi And Others vs U.P.S.R.T.C. Thru A.R.M. Deoria Depot on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134668307/
2 IV) Total annual income = Rs.36,000/- + Rs.14,400/- = Rs.50,400/- V) Deduction towards personal expenses(1/4th)=Rs.50,400/- - Rs.12,600/- = Rs.37,800/- VI)
Multiplier applicable (15) =Rs.37,800/- x 15 = Rs.5,67,000/- VII) Non-pecuniary damages = Rs.70,000/-
Total = Rs.5,67,000/- + Rs.70,000/- = Rs.6,37,000/-
9.

In view of aforesaid discussion, the first appeal from order filed by claimants is hereby partly allowed and award of the Claims Tribunal is modified and compensation is enhanced from Rs.2,57,751/- to Rs.6,37,000/-.

The claimants-appellants are also entitled for 6% interest on enhanced amount from the date of award of Claims Tribunal i.e. 08.12.2009.
10.

The U.P.S.R.T.C./opposite party is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.3,79,249/-
along with interest within two months from today before the concerned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

The claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire deposited amount without furnishing any surety.
11. No order as to costs.
